1	# Chess Roulette 🎮♟️
2	
3	A real-time online chess game with random matchmaking and live webcam video streaming. Think video-chat roulette, but across a chessboard.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	✅ **Hosted Server** - Runs online on a server both players reach over the internet  
8	✅ **Live 1v1 Chess** - Two players play a complete, rule-valid game in real time  
9	✅ **Random Matchmaking** - Players are matched randomly from the queue  
10	✅ **Webcam Video** - Live video streaming between opponents during the match  
11	✅ **Real-time Chat** - Text chat during the game  
12	✅ **Move Validation** - All moves are validated using chess.js  
13	
14	## Tech Stack
15	
16	- **Frontend**: React 18, TypeScript, Vite
17	- **Chess Logic**: chess.js, react-chessboard
18	- **Real-time Communication**: Socket.io
19	- **Video Streaming**: WebRTC
20	- **Backend**: Node.js, Express, Socket.io
21	
22	## Project Structure
23	
24	```
25	chess-roulette/
26	├── src/                    # Frontend React code
27	│   ├── components/         # React components
28	│   │   ├── ChessBoardPanel.tsx
29	│   │   ├── VideoPanel.tsx
30	│   │   ├── ChatPanel.tsx
31	│   │   └── Controls.tsx
32	│   ├── context/            # React Context
33	│   │   └── GameContext.tsx
34	│   ├── services/           # Socket.io & WebRTC services
35	│   │   ├── socket.ts
36	│   │   └── webrtc.ts
37	│   ├── types/              # TypeScript types
38	│   │   └── index.ts
39	│   ├── App.tsx
40	│   └── App.css
41	├── server/                 # Backend Node.js server
42	│   └── index.js
43	├── package.json
44	└── README.md
45	```
46	
47	## Setup Instructions
48	
49	### Prerequisites
50	
51	- Node.js v16+ and npm
52	- Modern web browser with WebRTC support
53	- Webcam and microphone
54	
55	### Installation
56	
57	1. **Install frontend dependencies:**
58	   ```bash
59	   npm install
60	   ```
61	
62	2. **Install server dependencies:**
63	   ```bash
64	   cd server
65	   npm install
66	   ```
67	
68	3. **Configure environment (optional):**
69	   ```bash
70	   # Copy .env.example to .env in the root directory
71	   cp .env.example .env
72	   ```
73	
74	### Running the Application
75	
76	You'll need two terminal windows:
77	
78	**Terminal 1 - Start the backend server:**
79	```bash
80	cd server
81	npm start
82	```
83	The server will start on `http://localhost:3001`
84	
85	**Terminal 2 - Start the frontend dev server:**
86	```bash
87	npm run dev
88	```
89	The frontend will start on `http://localhost:5173`
90	
91	### How to Play
92	
93	1. Open `http://localhost:5173` in your browser
94	2. Click **"Find Match"** to join the matchmaking queue
95	3. Wait for a random opponent to be found
96	4. Once matched, grant camera/microphone permissions
97	5. Play chess! White moves first
98	6. Use the chat to communicate with your opponent
99	7. First to checkmate wins, or you can resign at any time
100	
101	### Game Controls
102	
103	- **Find Match**: Join the random matchmaking queue
104	- **Camera On/Off**: Toggle your video stream
105	- **Mic On/Muted**: Toggle your audio
106	- **Switch Camera**: Switch between front/back cameras
107	- **Resign**: Forfeit the game
108	- **Disconnect**: Leave the game and disconnect from server
109	
110	## How It Works
111	
112	### Matchmaking
113	- Players join a queue via Socket.io
114	- When 2 players are in the queue, they're randomly paired
115	- One player is assigned white, the other black
116	- Game starts automatically after a brief delay
117	
118	### Chess Gameplay
119	- Moves are validated server-side using chess.js
120	- Move data is synced in real-time via Socket.io
121	- Board orientation adjusts based on your color
122	- Game detects checkmate, stalemate, and draws
123	
124	### Video Streaming (WebRTC)
125	- Peer-to-peer video connection between players
126	- Signaling happens through the Socket.io server
127	- Uses Google's STUN servers for NAT traversal
128	- Video and audio can be toggled during the game
129	
130	### Chat
131	- Real-time text chat during the game
132	- Messages are relayed through the server
133	- Chat history is maintained per game session
134	
135	## Deployment
136	
137	### Backend Deployment
138	
139	The server can be deployed to any Node.js hosting platform:
140	
141	- **Heroku**: Add a Procfile with `web: node server/index.js`
142	- **Railway**: Connect your repo and set the start command
143	- **DigitalOcean**: Deploy as a Node.js app
144	- **AWS**: Use EC2 or Elastic Beanstalk
145	
146	Make sure to set the `CLIENT_URL` environment variable to your frontend URL.
147	
148	### Frontend Deployment
149	
150	Build the frontend for production:
151	
152	```bash
153	npm run build
154	```
155	
156	Deploy the `dist` folder to:
157	
158	- **Vercel**: Auto-deploys from Git
159	- **Netlify**: Drag and drop or connect Git
160	- **GitHub Pages**: Use gh-pages package
161	- **Cloudflare Pages**: Connect Git repository
162	
163	Update `VITE_SERVER_URL` in `.env` to point to your deployed backend.
164	
165	## Troubleshooting
166	
167	### Camera/Microphone Issues
168	- Ensure you've granted browser permissions
169	- Check that no other app is using your camera
170	- Try refreshing the page
171	- Some browsers require HTTPS for WebRTC (except localhost)
172	
173	### Connection Issues
174	- Make sure both frontend and backend servers are running
175	- Check that the server URL in `.env` is correct
176	- Verify firewall settings allow connections on port 3001
177	
178	### Move Validation Errors
179	- Ensure you're making legal chess moves
180	- Wait for your turn (you can only move when it's your turn)
181	- The game enforces standard chess rules
182	
183	## Future Enhancements
184	
185	- [ ] Player ratings and matchmaking by skill level
186	- [ ] Game history and replay feature
187	- [ ] Timed games with chess clocks
188	- [ ] Spectator mode
189	- [ ] Tournament mode
190	- [ ] Custom board themes
191	- [ ] Move annotations and analysis
192	- [ ] Friend invites and private games
193	
194	## License
195	
196	MIT License - feel free to use this for learning or building your own chess platform!
197	
198	## Credits
199	
200	Built as part of a coding challenge demonstrating real-time web application development with React, TypeScript, Socket.io, and WebRTC.
